CVE-2026-106451.title: yawkat LZ4 Java: Native library extraction to a shared temporary directory is vulnerable to file replacement by another local user
CVE-2026-106451.description: yawkat LZ4 Java provides LZ4 compression for Java. From 1.7.0 until 1.11.4, net.jpountz.util.Native.load() uses File.createTempFile to create an exclusive temporary .lck file but derives the native-library path by removing the suffix, then FileOutputStream opens that predictable path without exclusive creation, allowing another local user with access to the same shared temporary directory to create or replace the library file before System.load() uses it. Successful exploitation depends on shared-directory permissions, host protections, and winning the race, and can execute native code as the victim; hardened systems may instead cause library loading to fail and fall back to Java implementations. Configurations using a system library, a private java.io.tmpdir, or Java-only implementations are not affected. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.4.

CVE-2026-116678.title: Vaultwarden: Icon endpoint SSRF fix bypass via second-stage favicon IP literal URLs
CVE-2026-116678.description: Vaultwarden is a Bitwarden-compatible server written in Rust. Prior to version 1.37.0, the Vaultwarden icon downloader validates the initial icon host and DNS results but passes favicon URLs parsed from attacker-controlled HTML to get_page_with_referer() without applying should_block_host() to the second-stage host. This flaw bypasses the remediation for CVE-2026-47160, which covered decimal, hexadecimal, octal, and IPv4-mapped IPv6 host normalization, because the second-stage IP-literal favicon fetch does not invoke the custom DNS resolver. A remote unauthenticated attacker can provide a public page whose favicon uses an IP-literal URL, allowing the Vaultwarden server to reach loopback or private and internal addresses. The issue affects instances with internal icon downloading enabled and can expose internal responses that resemble supported images or reveal reachability through timing, status, and cache behavior. This issue is fixed in version 1.37.0.

CVE-2026-53157.title: net: phonet: free phonet_device after RCU grace period
CVE-2026-53157.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: phonet: free phonet_device after RCU grace period

phonet_device_destroy() removes a phonet_device from the per-net device
list with list_del_rcu(), but frees it immediately. RCU readers walking
the same list can still hold a pointer to the object after it has been
removed, leading to a slab-use-after-free.

Use kfree_rcu(), matching the lifetime rule already used by
phonet_address_del() for the same object type.

CVE-2026-61619.title: OWASP CRS: ReDoS in shared unix-shell-evasion regex-assembly include (12 RCE rules) - PCRE2 backtracking-limit exhaustion causes detection bypass and CPU DoS
CVE-2026-61619.description: The OWASP core rule set (CRS) is a set of generic attack detection rules for use with compatible web application firewalls. Prior to versions 3.3.10, 4.25.1, and 4.28.0, regular-expression denial of service (ReDoS) affects a shared regex-assembly include used to build 12 Unix RCE detection rules in CRS v4, and the same ambiguous pattern was present in the manually-assembled regexes in 4 rules in CRS v3.3. With a single, unauthenticated, crafted request, the generated pattern drives PCRE2 past its backtracking limit. When PCRE2 exceeds that limit, the @rx operator returns an error rather than a match result, which results in detection bypass and CPU denial of service. This issue has been patched in versions 3.3.10, 4.25.1, and 4.28.0.

CVE-2026-76101.title: keystore-go: Keystore integrity and password verification bypass via stripped trailing digest in Decode(), impacting legacy v2 versions
CVE-2026-76101.description: keystore-go is a Go implementation of the Java KeyStore encoder and decoder. In 2.1.0 and earlier, keystore.Decode in decoder.go does not check the error returned when reading the trailing SHA-1 integrity digest and bounds its comparison by the length of the digest actually read. If an attacker with write access removes the final 20-byte digest from a modified JKS file, the empty actual digest causes the comparison loop to execute zero times and Decode returns the parsed keystore without an error. For certificate-only stores using TrustedCertificateEntry values, this bypasses both tamper detection and password verification, allowing trusted CA certificates to be added or replaced without knowing the keystore password and potentially enabling interception or modification of TLS connections that trust the forged CA. This issue is fixed in version 3.0.0.

CVE-2026-97401.description:
In Kura versions <= 5.6.2, `CommandCloudApp.execute()` extracts a caller-supplied ZIP archive into a caller-supplied directory inside the Kura JVM process before dispatching the command to the executor service. On a packaged Kura installation the JVM runs as `kurad` with `CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE`, while the configurable "Unprivileged" executor drops to the `kura` user via `su`.

A caller with permissions `rest.command` who is intentionally restricted to unprivileged command execution (`privileged.command.service.enable=false`, the default) can therefore set `workingDirectory` to `/` and use the ZIP body to write or overwrite arbitrary files on the device as `kurad`, completely bypassing the unprivileged sandbox the operator selected.

The command service is disabled by default since Kura 4.0.0 [1]. The issue does not apply when the command service is disabled.

[1] https://github.com/eclipse-kura/kura/blob/f9f969231892769a269876b23f19fa0e8173e3df/kura/distrib/RELEASE_NOTES.txt#L94

a spinlock and a wait queue. dm cache already has a wait queue and
